clue.text: Char is lady's polisher

parts.note: to char something is to burn it
a lady's belongings are hers, giving the possessive pronoun

explanation.surface: A cleaning woman turns out to be the household's polisher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' looks like a charwoman, the British cleaner, which suits a polisher; here it is the verb meaning to scorch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who burnishes rubs metal until it shines, so a polisher.

clue.text: Starts to bid up the going rate for paper

indicators.note: the starts of the words bid and up are their opening letters only

parts.note: MPH, miles per hour, is the rate at which a vehicle is going

explanation.surface: Bidding pushes up the going rate for paper at an auction.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang the answer means paperwork or official forms, often unwanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for documents and printed paperwork, especially tedious leaflets and forms.

clue.text: I roll about and make merry

indicators.note: the roll goes about, or around, the letter I

parts.note: a roll of names is a roster

explanation.surface: Someone rolling about in merriment says they mean to make merry.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel noisily and boisterously is to celebrate, to have a riotous good time.

clue.text: Envelope Uncle Ivor crumpled

indicators.note: crumpled means squashed out of shape, so the letters of the two names are rearranged

explanation.surface: An envelope addressed to Uncle Ivor got crumpled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Envelope' looks like a letter's cover but is the botanical sense: a ring of bracts around a flower head.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a whorl of bracts encasing a flower cluster is its envelope or sheath.

clue.text: Manual set down, but not in type

parts.note: manual means done by hand
to set something down on paper is to have it written

explanation.surface: A manual was set down on paper rather than typeset.
explanation.definitionFit: Script produced with a pen rather than printed lettering is not in type.

clue.text: The commercial theatre

definitions.meaning: a commercial traveller, a salesman on the road
repertory theatre, a company playing a changing programme

explanation.surface: The commercial theatre is the kind that sells tickets for profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial traveller is a sales representative; repertory theatre is shortened the same way.

clue.text: The end of the Hamlet-Horatio relationship

indicators.note: only the closing run of letters of the hyphenated pair of names is taken

explanation.surface: A reader wonders how the friendship between Hamlet and Horatio ends in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is the proportional relationship between two quantities.

clue.text: Railwaymen's approach to an event

parts.note: the old British rail union's initials, NUR, read upwards in this down entry give the first piece

explanation.surface: Railway workers prepare for a big event.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: NUR (the old British National Union of Railwaymen) going UP in a down light reads as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The run-up is the period of preparation leading to an occasion.

clue.text: Carrying merchandise up river in the middle of Rangoon

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the river's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon

indicators.note: the central letter of the seven-letter city name is taken

explanation.surface: Boats carry goods up the river through the centre of Rangoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing in and shipping goods for sale is commerce, buying and selling.

clue.text: It gives the striker extra to carry out subversion

definitions.meaning: in cricket a misfielded return lets the batting striker run again

explanation.surface: Something gives a strike leader extra means to carry out subversion.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a fielder's wild return past the stumps lets the batsman, the striker, take extra runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket fielding error giving bonus runs; also the toppling of a government by force.

clue.text: Vehicle with defensive armour for communication duties?

parts.note: chain mail is defensive armour
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An armoured vehicle is being fitted out for signals work.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: a post office van carries letters, so it works in communications.
explanation.definitionFit: Post office vans carry letters, the business of correspondence.

clue.text: Step outside the pub for a gig

indicators.note: the step goes outside, around, the pub

parts.note: a pace is a step
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A band member steps outside the pub before a gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gig' suggests a concert; it is also a light ship's boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are light ship's boats, the gig rowed and the larger one often sailed.

clue.text: Rent return on house put up here

indicators.note: in an across clue on means the reversed piece follows the house
return means the word for rent is read backwards

parts.note: to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: A landlord gets a return on a house by putting it up for rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Guests are lodged, or put up, at an inn for the night.

clue.text: Mae takes the stage for the American Academy

parts.note: Mae West, the American film actress
a point is a stage, as in a point in the proceedings

explanation.surface: Mae West takes to the stage at an American drama academy.
explanation.definitionFit: The US Military Academy on the Hudson is known by this location's name.

clue.text: Robber gets out of danger on a ' white horse

parts.note: safe means out of danger
white horses are breaking waves, so a breaker

explanation.surface: A robber escapes danger by riding off on a white horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White horse' is not a mount but a foam-crested wave; 'on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cracksman who opens strongboxes is a kind of thief.

clue.text: Douglas, perhaps, cut for deal

definitions.meaning: the Douglas is one kind of conifer
deal is softwood planking sawn from conifers

explanation.surface: Douglas tries to cut a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas is a species of conifer, not a person; deal is softwood timber, not an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Douglas is a conifer species, and deal is sawn softwood timber from such trees.

clue.text: Novel epithet, though not true

definitions.meaning: an adjective meaning of or in a novel

explanation.surface: A novel adjective is coined, though it is untrue.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes something belonging to novels, and also anything invented rather than real.

clue.text: Lear's samphire-gatherer in an uncertain situation

definitions.meaning: the figure Edgar pictures dangling from the Dover rocks
a suspenseful state whose outcome is unknown

explanation.surface: A character in King Lear is caught in an uncertain situation.
explanation.walkthrough: In King Lear, Edgar describes a man halfway down the Dover cliffs gathering samphire, a coastal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The man dangling from the rock face in Lear, and a tense unresolved state of suspense.

clue.text: Drink in private? That's madness!

indicators.note: madness suggests the letters have gone crazy and must be rearranged

parts.note: i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Someone drinking in private is told that this is madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetiser drink taken before a meal, such as sherry.

clue.text: Car that can be traded in

definitions.meaning: a motor car with a folding roof
exchangeable for something of equal value

explanation.surface: A car that can be part-exchanged at the dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft-top car, and something exchangeable for money or other goods.

clue.text: Units on manoeuvres get order to stop action

indicators.note: military units on manoeuvres move about, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Units on exercise are ordered to halt the action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on manoeuvres' carries the fodder word 'on'; the anagram signal is 'manoeuvres'. The 'action' is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's ruling ending a lawsuit because the plaintiff failed to make a case.

clue.text: Bloody, but fighting back

indicators.note: back means the word for fighting is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: war is fighting

explanation.surface: Someone is bloodied but keeps fighting back.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw meat or a raw wound is red and bleeding.

clue.text: The King is also Emperor, of course

parts.note: R, from Rex, stands for king
Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors

explanation.surface: The king is also an emperor, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but 'course' is a dish in a meal; 'also' and 'of' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice dish served as one part of a meal.

clue.text: The spotless condition of Father Brown's book

explanation.surface: A priest's book describes a spotless state of the soul.
explanation.walkthrough: The Innocence of Father Brown is G.K. Chesterton's first collection of stories about his priest detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Purity or freedom from guilt, and the title word of Chesterton's first detective collection.

clue.text: Anna, say, accepts Rex as swain

indicators.note: the coin accepts, takes in, the letter for king

parts.note: an anna was a coin of British India
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: Anna accepts a king as her suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anna' is not a woman but an old Indian coin; the answer is the old shepherd in As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: A shepherd in Shakespeare's As You Like It, a country lad or rustic lover.

clue.text: Extra page for popular series of games

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
in tennis a set is a series of games

explanation.surface: A popular games series earns an extra page in the magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose sheet or extra leaf placed inside a publication.

clue.text: Initial letter in Tamil language is short

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word Tamil is taken

parts.note: Erse is Gaelic, a language

explanation.surface: The first letter of the Tamil alphabet is a short one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tamil language' reads as one phrase; Tamil only gives its first letter and the language is Erse (Gaelic).
explanation.definitionFit: Brief and curt in speech or writing.

clue.text: Gear for those going to coast

definitions.text: Gear for those going to coast

parts.words: Gear for those going to coast
parts.note: the gearbox position, with no gear engaged, used when freewheeling downhill, not kit for seaside trippers

explanation.surface: Kit packed for a trip to the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coast' looks like the seaside but is the verb: to roll along without power.
explanation.definitionFit: The disengaged gear position lets a car freewheel without drive.

clue.text: Highball makes one throw up

definitions.meaning: a ball sent high in the air

explanation.surface: A strong whisky drink makes one sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highball' looks like a whisky cocktail and 'throw up' like vomiting; both are about tossing a ball high.
explanation.definitionFit: A high lofted ball in tennis or cricket, and to toss something high.

clue.text: Royal kitten distracted by one with ball of wool

indicators.note: a distracted kitten is all over the place, so its letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A royal kitten is distracted by someone holding a ball of wool.
explanation.walkthrough: The R from 'Royal' sits after the anagram of KITTEN; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person making garments with needles works from a ball of yarn.

clue.text: Language the French can make up

parts.note: la is a French word for the
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: The French can make up a language.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of ancient Rome.

clue.text: With which people kept their distance from the Untouchables?

definitions.text: With which people kept their distance from the Untouchables?

parts.words: With which people kept their distance from the Untouchables?
parts.note: plays on the idiom of refusing to touch something with a long boat pole, applied to people literally untouchable

explanation.surface: Asks how people avoided the Untouchables, an outcast group or Eliot Ness's agents.
explanation.walkthrough: People say they 'wouldn't touch it with a' long pole used to push a barge; the joke takes 'Untouchables' literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pole for propelling a flat boat, used idiomatically for things one refuses to touch.
